haiku-low.q1: The old engine charges and writes the ledger. The new engine's output goes to the shadow store, and it never calls the payment provider.
haiku-low.q2: The new engine charges and writes the ledger. The old engine computes invoices into the shadow store and never calls the payment provider.
haiku-low.q3: Gate A: the last 7 consecutive days each have under 0.1% mismatches, totaling at least 5,000 invoices, counted since the latest entry into shadow. On-call promotes via the rollout tool.
haiku-low.q4: The billing monitor starts it automatically when the new engine's payment-call failure rate exceeds 2% over 10 minutes. This happens only in both or new_only mode.
haiku-low.q5: Every rollback ends in old_only. Before the new engine can take over, on-call must promote to shadow and gate A must be met from scratch.
haiku-low.q6: Once 35 days have passed since new_only began. Usage events are kept only 35 days, so catch-up needs the log, and the rollout tool then rejects all rollbacks.
haiku-low.q7: Workers read billing_mode at the start of each invoice, so an in-progress invoice finishes in its starting mode. They read charging_paused before every payment call, so a pause applies at the next charge.
haiku-low.q8: In the nightly comparison_results rows. The rollout tool checks them before writing billing_mode and refuses any promotion that skips a mode or fails its gate.
haiku-low.q9: The billing monitor. It measures the new engine's payment-provider call failure rate over a 10-minute sliding window. Above 2% in both or new_only, it starts a rollback and pages on-call.
haiku-low.q10: Charges falling due are written to the ledger as pending, not charged. They are charged later, when the old engine resumes charging after charging_paused is set to false.
haiku-low.q11: Reconcile: an invoice already charged with matching totals is marked settled and never charged again. Mismatched totals go to the Finance review queue, not re-charged automatically.
haiku-low.q12: Billing stays in rolling_back with charging paused, and the new engine never resumes charging. On-call is paged, and the step is retried from the rollback record, since steps are safe to repeat.

sonnet.q1: The old engine charges and writes the ledger. The new engine computes into the shadow store.
sonnet.q2: The new engine charges and writes the ledger. The old engine computes into the shadow store.
sonnet.q3: Gate A must be met: each of the last 7 consecutive days has a mismatch rate under 0.1%, and together those days compared at least 5,000 invoices. On-call promotes, and the rollout tool refuses the move if the gate fails.
sonnet.q4: The billing monitor starts it automatically when the new engine's payment-provider failure rate goes above 2% over a sliding 10-minute window. This happens only in `both` or `new_only` (and in new_only only within 35 days of entering it). It also pages on-call.
sonnet.q5: Every rollback ends in `old_only`. To take over again, on-call must promote to `shadow` and gate A must be met from scratch, then proceed through both and gate B.
sonnet.q6: It stops once 35 days have passed since `new_only` began. Usage events are kept only 35 days, so catch-up only works while every event since new_only began is still in the log. After that the tool rejects all rollbacks, and the monitor only pages on-call.
sonnet.q7: Workers read `billing_mode` at the start of each invoice. An invoice already in progress finishes under the mode it started in.
sonnet.q8: In the `comparison_results` table, where the nightly comparison job writes one row per day. Gate B also needs a Finance sign-off recorded in the rollout tool. The rollout tool checks these rows before writing `billing_mode` and refuses any promotion that skips a mode or fails its gate.
sonnet.q9: The billing monitor. It measures the failure rate of the new engine's payment-provider calls over a sliding 10-minute window. If the rate goes above 2% in `both` or `new_only`, it starts a rollback through the rollout tool and pages on-call.
sonnet.q10: Once `charging_paused` is true, invoices that fall due are written to the ledger as pending instead of being charged. A call already in flight finishes and is recorded. The old engine charges the pending invoices at the resume_charging step, when `charging_paused` is set to false.
sonnet.q11: The reconcile step matches each new-engine ledger invoice with the old engine's invoice for the same customer and billing period. If it was already charged and the totals agree, it is marked settled and never charged again. If the totals differ, it goes to the Finance review queue and is not re-charged automatically.
sonnet.q12: The rollout stays in `rolling_back`. Charging stays paused and the new engine never gets charging back. On-call is paged, and the step is retried from the rollback record. Steps are safe to repeat, so charges are delayed but never dropped or doubled.
